Run through lemonbeam's own pipeline (MVP_MODEL currently openai/gpt-5.6-luna), chosen specifically to verify the CI/Compose yml classification fix against a real repo that has both .github/workflows/*.yml AND a root docker-compose.yml -- express (tested earlier) only had the former.

CI half of the fix confirmed working end-to-end in this live guide: real citations to [.github/workflows/mutation-test.yml] (Setup and Testing sections) and [.github/workflows/tests-windows.yml] (Testing section) appear in the generated markdown, not just in a backend-only check.

Compose half: docker-compose.yml is never directly cited in the guide text -- the one Docker Compose mention in Setup cites DEVELOPER.md instead. Followed up with the same backend-only discover->classify->chunk->score->budget check used on express (bypassing the LLM call), run directly against a fresh clone of this repo. Result: docker-compose.yml IS classified as config, chunked as compose_config, and scores correctly (setup: 1, running: 1) -- the fix's classification/scoring machinery is confirmed working. It was excluded at the budgeting step purely because Setup's 9,000-token budget filled up with other evidence (DEVELOPER.md, package.json, ormconfig.sample.json, etc.) before reaching it -- same fate as 4 of the 11 real CI workflow files (pr-triage.yml, publish-package.yml, tests-linux.yml, tests.yml). This is a budget-tuning question, not a bug in the classification/scoring fix -- confirms the Uncertainties section's generic 'excluded (irrelevant or over budget)' message really can mean 'ran out of room', distinct from the zero-relevance case the fix targeted.

Unrelated finding, same repo: the tree-sitter 32KB 'Invalid argument' chunking bug (first seen on the moment repo test) shows up much more here -- 42 files listed as unanalyzable, vs. 9 on moment. Further evidence this is a broadly-impactful issue worth prioritizing, not a one-off.

Citations were not independently hand-verified against the real repo for this run -- worth a spot-check before treating this as fully validated.

## Project Overview

TypeORM is a TypeScript-based Object-Relational Mapping library for Node.js, browsers, React Native, Cordova, Ionic, NativeScript, Expo, and Electron. [docs/docs/getting-started.md:1-21] It supports Active Record and Data Mapper patterns and provides database drivers for Google Spanner, Microsoft SQL Server, MongoDB, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SAP HANA, and SQLite. [docs/docs/getting-started.md:1-21]

The repository is primarily a TypeScript library targeting CommonJS and modern JavaScript, with decorators enabled for entity metadata. [tsconfig.json] [tsconfig.json] The package description identifies it as a Data Mapper ORM supporting TypeScript and ES2023+. [package.json]

The main implementation is under `src/`, with `DataSource` managing database configuration, drivers, entity managers, repositories, query runners, and caching. [src/data-source/DataSource.ts:57-132] [src/data-source/DataSource.ts:192-194] The repository also includes a Docusaurus documentation website, an `@typeorm/codemod` migration tool, legacy naming strategies, and a SQLite/sql.js playground. [docs/README.md:1-4] [packages/codemod/README.md:1-4] [packages/legacy-naming-strategies/README.md:1-2] [playground/README.md:1-18]

Likely development entry points are the root build scripts, the TypeORM CLI documented under `docs/docs/using-cli.md`, the documentation site under `docs/`, and the playground application under `playground/`. [package.json] [docs/docs/using-cli.md:1-11] [docs/package.json] [playground/package.json]

## Setup / Installation

The documented prerequisites include Git, Node.js, and database services for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server; Docker can provide local database services. [DEVELOPER.md:8-26] The package declares supported Node.js versions as `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24.11.0`. [package.json] The documentation also states that TypeORM is compatible with Node.js 20+ and tests commits on Node.js 20 and 24. [docs/docs/help/2-supported-platforms.md:3-6]

The repository uses `pnpm` for dependency installation. [DEVELOPER.md:47-54] Install root dependencies with:

```shell
pnpm install
```

[DEVELOPER.md:47-54]

Create the initial ORM configuration by copying the sample configuration file:

```shell
cp ormconfig.sample.json ormconfig.json
```

[DEVELOPER.md:55-62] Database connection parameters must then be configured in `ormconfig.json`, and the test suite runs against the database definitions present in that file. [DEVELOPER.md:84-140]

Docker Compose can be used to start the documented PostgreSQL service with:

```shell
docker compose up postgres-17
```

[DEVELOPER.md:8-26] The evidence also shows CI database services using MySQL on port `3306`, MariaDB on host port `3307`, and PostgreSQL on port `5432`. [ .github/workflows/mutation-test.yml] These ports are shown for CI services and are not documented as application-server ports. [ .github/workflows/mutation-test.yml]

The evidence does not show a required root `.env` file or root environment-variable setup. [docs/releases/1.0/02-upgrading-from-0.3.md:411-425] TypeORM no longer auto-loads `.env` files or legacy `TYPEORM_*` connection variables; configuration should use a TypeScript or JavaScript configuration file instead. [docs/releases/1.0/02-upgrading-from-0.3.md:411-425]

For the documentation site, install dependencies from the `docs/` directory with `pnpm install`. [docs/README.md:5-10] The documentation package requires Node.js `>=20.0`. [docs/package.json]

## Running Locally

The root package exposes scripts for compilation, packaging, linting, formatting, type checking, watching, and testing. [package.json] Build the core project with:

```shell
pnpm run compile
```

[package.json] This runs the Gulp clean task followed by TypeScript compilation. [package.json] A watch mode is available with:

```shell
pnpm run watch
```

[package.json]

The documented fast development cycle is to run `pnpm run compile -- --watch`, then use `pnpm run test:fast` while editing. [DEVELOPER.md:157-164] The normal `pnpm run test` script recompiles the codebase before running tests, while `pnpm run test:fast` runs tests without the full recompile. [DEVELOPER.md:157-164] [package.json]

The documentation website runs from `docs/` with:

```shell
pnpm run start
```

[docs/README.md:11-18] Its build command is:

```shell
pnpm run build
```

[docs/README.md:19-26] The root repository provides a convenience command for this workflow:

```shell
pnpm run docs:dev
```

[package.json]

The playground can be installed and started with `npm i` followed by `npm start`. [playground/README.md:1-7] Its `start` script runs `node --loader ts-node/esm src/index.ts`, and its `build` script runs `tsc`. [playground/package.json] The playground uses an in-memory sql.js SQLite database and therefore does not require a database server. [playground/README.md:8-18] [playground/README.md:51-55]

The supplied evidence does not show a root application start script or an application development server port. [package.json] The visible local servers are the Docusaurus development server and the playground process, but no explicit port is provided for either in the supplied files. [docs/README.md:11-18] [playground/package.json]

## Project Structure

- `src/` contains the core TypeORM implementation. [tsconfig.json]
- `src/data-source/` defines data-source configuration and the `DataSource` abstraction. [src/data-source/DataSource.ts:57-132] [src/data-source/BaseDataSourceOptions.ts:71-78]
- `src/driver/` contains database-specific implementations; the repository guidance states that each driver handles connection management, query execution, schema synchronization, type mapping, and transactions. [.github/copilot-instructions.md:129-150]
- `src/decorator/` contains decorator implementations and decorator option types for columns, relations, indexes, transactions, and constraints. [src/decorator/columns/PrimaryGeneratedColumn.ts:83-85] [src/decorator/options/ColumnOptions.ts:53-131]
- `src/metadata/` and `src/metadata-args/` represent entity, relation, index, constraint, and decorator metadata. [src/metadata-args/MetadataArgsStorage.ts:30-48] [src/metadata/RelationMetadata.ts:21-23]
- `src/metadata-builder/` builds entity and relation metadata used by the ORM. [src/metadata-builder/JunctionEntityMetadataBuilder.ts:20-23] [src/metadata-builder/RelationJoinColumnBuilder.ts:51-54]
- `src/repository/` contains repository abstractions, including standard, tree, MongoDB, and Active Record repositories. [src/repository/Repository.ts:40-56] [src/repository/MongoRepository.ts:53-75] [src/repository/TreeRepository.ts:18-44]
- `src/query-builder/` contains query-builder classes and query-expression structures for select, insert, update, delete, soft-delete, and relation operations. [src/query-builder/DeleteQueryBuilder.ts:19-39] [src/query-builder/UpdateQueryBuilder.ts:32-52] [src/query-builder/QueryExpressionMap.ts:23-40]
- `src/migration/` contains migration execution logic. [src/migration/MigrationExecutor.ts:15-45] The project guidance states that migrations belong in `src/migration/`, should be timestamped, and should support reversible `up` and `down` operations. [.github/copilot-instructions.md:171-178]
- `src/schema-builder/` contains schema, table, column, index, key, constraint, and view representations. [src/schema-builder/table/Table.ts:16-66] [src/schema-builder/view/View.ts:12-49]
- `src/cache/`, `src/logger/`, `src/query-runner/`, `src/entity-manager/`, `src/persistence/`, and `src/subscriber/` provide caching, logging, connection-level query execution, entity operations, persistence, and lifecycle-event support. [src/cache/QueryResultCacheFactory.ts:15-15] [src/query-runner/QueryRunner.ts:33-96] [src/subscriber/EntitySubscriberInterface.ts:122-124]
- `test/` contains benchmark, core, functional, GitHub issue, other-issue, and unit tests. [test/benchmark/bulk-save-case1/bulk-save-case1.test.ts:18-18] [test/core/column-kinds/create-date-column/create-date-column.test.ts:19-19] [test/unit/cache/redis-query-result-cache.test.ts:27-29]
- `docs/` is a Docusaurus website containing guides, API documentation, driver documentation, migration documentation, and release notes. [docs/README.md:1-4] [docs/docs/getting-started.md:1-21]
- `packages/codemod/` is a separate TypeScript package for automated TypeORM version migrations. [packages/codemod/README.md:1-4] `packages/legacy-naming-strategies/` provides legacy naming strategy implementations. [packages/legacy-naming-strategies/README.md:23-39]
- `playground/` contains an ESM sql.js example application with TypeScript source under `playground/src/`. [playground/README.md:8-18] [playground/package.json]

## Testing

The root test framework is Mocha, with Chai and related assertion packages visible in the development dependencies. [package.json] The root test commands are:

```shell
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:fast
pnpm run test:ci
```

[package.json] `test` compiles the project and then invokes the fast test command, `test:fast` runs `mocha`, and `test:ci` runs `mocha --bail`. [package.json]

Tests are organized primarily under `test/benchmark/`, `test/core/`, `test/functional/`, `test/github-issues/`, `test/other-issues/`, and `test/unit/`. [test/benchmark/bulk-save-case1/bulk-save-case1.test.ts:18-18] [test/core/column-kinds/create-date-column/create-date-column.test.ts:19-19] [test/functional/data-source/data-source.test.ts:123-123] [test/unit/cache/redis-query-result-cache.test.ts:27-29] Functional tests cover areas including persistence, relations, query builders, schema building, drivers, migrations, transactions, tree tables, and GitHub issue regressions. [test/functional/persistence/persistence-basic-functionality.test.ts:19-19] [test/functional/query-builder/delete/query-builder-delete.test.ts:20-20] [test/functional/schema-builder/collation/collation-changes/collation-changes.test.ts:25-25] [test/functional/transaction/isolation-level/postgres-isolation.test.ts:38-38]

Most database-oriented tests use shared testing utilities to create connections and reload testing databases before each test. [DEVELOPER.md:84-140] The visible functional test pattern commonly calls `reloadTestingDatabases(dataSources)` in `beforeEach`. [test/functional/persistence/persistence-basic-functionality/persistence-basic-functionality.test.ts:19-19] Tests commonly define entities in nearby `entity/` directories, and the developer guide states that entities placed in `./entity/<entity-name>.ts` relative to a test are automatically loaded. [DEVELOPER.md:84-140]

Database tests require `ormconfig.json`, created from `ormconfig.sample.json`, and run for each database configured there. [DEVELOPER.md:84-140] CI also generates filtered `ormconfig.json` files for selected drivers and runs commands such as `pnpm exec c8 pnpm run test:ci`. [.github/workflows/tests-windows.yml] The mutation-testing workflow uses `pnpm exec stryker run`. [.github/workflows/mutation-test.yml]

The codemod package has its own Mocha-based test script and tests under `packages/codemod/test/`, including CLI tests, transform tests, and input/output fixture files. [packages/codemod/package.json] [packages/codemod/test/cli/list-transforms.test.ts:12-14] [packages/codemod/test/transforms/ast-helpers.test.ts:297-297] The legacy naming strategies package also exposes a Mocha test script. [packages/legacy-naming-strategies/package.json]
